README:  --> # Model Overview ## Description: NVIDIA Isaac GR00T N1.7 is an open foundation model for generalized humanoid robot reasoning and skills. This cross-embodiment model takes multimodal input, including language and images, to perform manipulation tasks in diverse environments. Developers and researchers can post-train GR00T N1.7 with real or synthetic data for their specific humanoid robot or task. Isaac GR00T N1.7 is the medium-sized version of our model built using pre-trained vision and language encoders, and uses a flow matching action transformer to model a chunk of actions conditioned on vision, language and proprioception. A detailed description of the Isaac GR00T N1.X architecture is provided in the GROOT N1 White Paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14734). This model is ready for commercial/non-commercial use. **Model Developer**: NVIDIA ## Model Versions The Isaac GR00T N1.7 model family includes the following 4 models: ### GR00T N1.7 – SimplerEnv Bridge **Description** N1.7 post-trained model using the **Bridge Dataset** in SimplerEnv. **Post-Training Data** https://huggingface.co/datasets/IPEC-COMMUNITY/bridge_orig_lerobot **Dataset Summary** A LeRobot-format conversion of **BridgeData V2**, originally containing **60,096 trajectories** of robot manipulation across **24 environments**. ### GR00T N1.7 – SimplerEnv Fractal **Description** N1.7 post-trained model using the **Fractal Dataset** in SimplerEnv. **Post-Training Data** https://huggingface.co/datasets/IPEC

cards.body: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. related.title: Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy further complicates Nvidia’s China problem

cards.body: Following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission on Sunday to an extramarital affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, the chipmaker's relationship to China is about to come under intense scrutiny in Washington, D.C. Since October 2022, when the Biden administration announced sweeping controls to limit China's ability to obtain advanced U.S. chips, Nvidia has seen its business diminish in the world's second-largest economy. Months after an even stricter set of rules was implemented by the Trump administration, Huang said in October 2025, "We are 100% out of China." The recent allegations against Huang, while throwing the chipmaker into crisis, have also brought attention to the Nvidia CEO's potential influence over U.S. policy on chip sales to China, where its business once flourished. Of particular interest is whether restricted Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies through customers like Singapore-based Megaspeed, the company linked to Alice Huang. The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring. China has called the allegation a smear. Jensen Huang has been closely aligned with President Donald Trump during his second administration, helping advise the White House on artificial intelligence safety regulations, while also pushing for looser restrictions on selling AI chips to China. In December, Trump said Nvidia would be allowed to ship its H200 chips to China, provided the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales. In March, Huang told reporters that Nvidia had "received purchase orders, and we're in the process of restarting our manufacturing." Huang was a last-minute addition to the roster of tech executives who joined Trump on a trip to China in May, after the president was briefed on intelligence concerns, according to the Times. "In 35 years, I haven't seen a chip CEO with this much direct influence on export policy," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO at Moor Insights & Strategy, in an email. Since last week's midterm elections that included sweeping victories across the country for Democrats, the mood in Washington has changed. Three House committees have requested closed-door briefings with the Nvidia CEO about his relationship with Megaspeed. Democratic lawmakers, who are about to take power in the House and Senate, have said publicly that Congress will investigate and seek answers. Trump said Monday that he was "amazed" by the allegations and that Huang told him he "had no idea that she was a spy." The FBI is now looking into the issue, Trump said at a White House briefing. 'Turbulent month or so' It's been a long four years for Nvidia in China. Before the initial export controls in 2022, China made up nearly a quarter of Nvidia's revenue. README:  --> # Model Overview ## Description: NVIDIA Isaac GR00T N1.7 is an open foundation model for generalized humanoid robot reasoning and skills. This cross-embodiment model takes multimodal input, including language and images, to perform manipulation tasks in diverse environments. Developers and researchers can post-train GR00T N1.7 with real or synthetic data for their specific humanoid robot or task. Isaac GR00T N1.7 is the medium-sized version of our model built using pre-trained vision and language encoders, and uses a flow matching action transformer to model a chunk of actions conditioned on vision, language and proprioception. A detailed description of the Isaac GR00T N1.X architecture is provided in the GROOT N1 White Paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14734). key_facts: AV 개발사들은 **온보드 시스템의 컴퓨팅·지연 시간 제약 내에서 작동하는 추론 모델**이 필요하다
대형 모델은 이러한 추론 능력의 기반을 제공하지만, 차량에 탑재하려면 모델 크기 축소·유용한 추론 능력 보존·타깃 하드웨어 성능 검증이라는 추가 작업이 필요하다
**NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge**가 이러한 과제를 해결한다고 언급됨
구체적 수치(모델 크기, 지연시간, 벤치마크 결과)는 본문에 없어 미확인
summary_data.why_matters: 자율주행 업계는 대형 추론 모델의 성능과 차량 탑재 가능한 경량화 사이의 트레이드오프라는 공통 과제를 안고 있다. **NVIDIA가 엣지 최적화 모델을 직접 제시**함으로써 AV 소프트웨어 스택에서의 기술 리더십과 end-to-end 솔루션 제공 범위를 확장하려는 움직임으로 해석된다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 클라우드/트레이닝용 대형 모델뿐 아니라 **차량 내 추론(in-vehicle inference)용 경량 모델까지 자체 제공**함으로써 AV 스택 전체(데이터센터 학습-차량 배포)를 아우르는 풀스택 전략을 강화하고 있다.
summary_data.focus_angle: 자동차 OEM과 자율주행 개발사 입장에서는 대형 추론 모델의 성능을 유지하면서도 차량 탑재형 컴퓨팅 자원 내에서 실시간으로 작동하는 모델 확보가 상용화의 핵심 관문이며, NVIDIA가 이 경량화·검증 과정을 플랫폼화해 제공할 경우 **자체 모델 최적화 역량이 부족한 OEM들의 자율주행 개발 진입장벽을 낮출 수 있다**.

README:  # Alpamayo 2 Edge [**Code**](https://github.com/NVlabs/alpamayo2-edge) | [**Alpamayo Overview**](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/autonomous-vehicles/alpamayo/) ## Model Overview: ### Description: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is a 2B-parameter reasoning vision-language-action model that uses adaptive reasoning to generate driving trajectories and causal explanations. Built on the Nemotron-based backbone of NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge, it supports fine-tuning and efficient in-vehicle deployment on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. Alpamayo 2 Edge was developed by NVIDIA as a part of the broader [Alpamayo Open Platform](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/autonomous-vehicles/alpamayo/). ### License/Terms of Use: **Model weights:** The model weights are released under the [OpenMDW-1.1](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/) license. **Source code:** Apache License 2.0, as provided in the [Alpamayo 2 Edge source repository](https://github.com/NVlabs/alpamayo2-edge). ### Deployment Geography: Global ### Use Case: Developers and researchers working on autonomous vehicle systems who need a compact reasoning model for in-vehicle planning and decision-making. Alpamayo 2 Edge generates navigation-conditioned driving trajectories together with causal explanations, and it can answer free-form questions about a driving scene. It serves as a starting point for fine-tuning and for efficient deployment on in-vehicle platforms. ### Release Date: **Hugging Face:** 11/10/2026 via https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Alpa

summary_data.focus_angle: **수술 로봇·로봇 초음파 등 의료용 자율 로봇 OEM이 NVIDIA의 범용 VLA를 기반으로 자사 embodiment에 맞춘 파인튜닝을 할 수 있는 선례**를 제공하며, 휴머노이드 중심이던 GR00T 플랫폼이 특수 목적 로봇(산업·의료·향후 자동차 관련 로보틱스)으로 확장 가능함을 시사한다.

headlines.body: Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform : NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine , NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot . These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future. Securing AI Agents in the Open NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF puts security infrastructure for autonomous agents in the community’s hands to build, inspect and improve — accelerating development and hardening its safeguards. “The cloud-native community has a new infrastructure challenge: giving agents secure environments in which to operate,” said Jim Zemlin, CEO of the Linux Foundation. “NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF gives developers a shared foundation to build on and an opportunity to shape how agent security evolves. Bringing this work into the community enables broader collaboration on infrastructure that will be critical to the next generation of cloud-native applications.” OpenShell gives organizations control over what AI agents can do. It applies deterministic controls to agent activity, so teams can enforce policies as agents use tools, access inference services and execute workloads. Its extensible architecture lets teams connect their own compute, inference providers, credential storage and monitoring tools. This allows organizations to apply governance across different deployment environments while integrating OpenShell with their existing enterprise systems. Hundreds of organizations have put OpenShell to use, and the project has received tens of thousands of contributions in less than a year since launch. headlines.body: Democratic leader Sen. Charles Schumer ripped President Donald Trump on Tuesday for defending embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the expense of U.S. national security. "The press reports that Trump was briefed more than a year ago that Nvidia's CEO was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and Trump didn't do anything – anything – about it," Schumer, D-N.Y., said on the Senate floor. "Can you believe that?" said Schumer, the Senate's minority leader. Schumer's broadside came on the heels of New York Times reports that Trump had been briefed about Huang's extramarital affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang — whom U.S. intelligence concluded was a spy for China — and opted not to do anything about it. Trump suggested to reporters on Monday that he only recently learned of the allegations about Alice Huang, and the president commented Monday that he "really" believes Jensen Huang's claim to him directly that he had no idea Alice Huang was a spy. "One of our most important companies that is involved in national security, and the CEO might be having an affair with a Chinese spy, and Trump did nothing about it," Schumer said Tuesday. "What a dereliction of duty. He's supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends," Schumer said. "Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be defending our national security. It's that simple, it's obvious." Schumer's comments escalated growing bipartisan concern in Congress about the Nvidia CEO and his company. Nvidia makes advanced chips that are essential components in developing artificial intelligence models, a sector that is the focus of keen competition between the United States and China. Schumer noted that Trump earlier this year invited Huang to join him on a state visit to Beijing, and that he took Huang's advice by granting the People's Republic of China "access to some of our most advanced AI chips." Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump's controversial White House ballroom project, the Democrat said. "Despite talking a big game, Trump continues to show a troubling resistance to confront China on AI and to protect American national security," Schumer said. "I've been saying it for years: our cutting-edge AI chips are too valuable to fall into the hands of potential adversaries." headlines.body: German telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom is expanding its AI data center in Munich. The company this week announced it will continue to expand its ‘AI factory’ data center at Munich's Tucherpark, expanding the site by 20MW. As well as continuing to use Nvidia’s RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition and B200s GPUs, the company will deploy additional Blackwell Ultra Generation (B300) GPUs at the facility. Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges said: “Germany must not only be a user of AI; it must also create value and prosperity itself. Telekom has moved forward here at a rapid pace. The world must take Europe seriously. The goal is not only to develop AI, but to put it into practice as a scalable business model – delivering measurable efficiency gains, new products, and additional value creation in Germany and Europe.” After announcing plans in October 2025, the Industrial AI Cloud (AI factory) at Munich's Tucherpark only went live in February 2026. DT said the initial deployment increased available AI computing capacity in Germany by 50 percent and was fully booked within seven months. SAP and Deutsche Telekom were among the companies pitching to host a large-scale data center as part of the European Union's AI gigafactory initiative. Munich is a prominent secondary market in Germany. A May 2024 market report by data center research firm DC Byte states that the city is the country’s third-largest market by capacity, behind Frankfurt and Berlin. Founded in 2000, Deutsche Telekom’s T-Systems has 130MW of data center capacity across 16 data centers. Its footprint spans facilities and private cloud regions in Germany (Munich, Frankfurt, Biere), Switzerland, Austria, the Netherlands, and the US. It launched a private cloud region in Spain in 2024. Digital Transformation Capital Partners (DTCP), which was spun out of Deutsche Telekom in 2015 but retains close ties to the telco, owns a majority stake in German data center operator Maincubes. It also recently took a stake in Irish data center firm Atlantic Hub.

headlines.body: AI 추천 뉴스 KAIST·엔비디아 "한국어 데이터 100만건 구축" 김현우 AI 공동연구소장 "피지컬·기업 생태계로 확장" 엔비디아와 KAIST가 인공지능(AI) 모델 학습에 활용할 한국어 특화 데이터를 내년까지 100만 건 이상 구축해 공개한다. 한국 AI 연구 생태계에 양질의 한국어 데이터를 공급해 국내 연구자가 모델 개발 등에 활용하도록 지원하고, 연구 생태계를 데이터·응용 서비스 등으로 넓힌다는 계획이다. 김현우 KAIST-엔비디아 AI공동연구소장(사진)은 10일 서울 삼성동 엔비디아코리아 사무실에서 진행된 인터뷰에서 연구 방향을 공유했다. KAIST와 엔비디아는 5년간 총 3억달러(약 4000억원)의 예산으로 AI를 연구하기 위해 지난 7월 공동연구소를 세웠다. 김 소장은 AI 생태계를 숲에 비유했다. 김 소장은 “AI 생태계는 다양한 요소가 어우러지는 아름다운 숲”이라며 “지금까지는 나무에 해당하는 AI 모델을 만드는 데 초점을 맞췄다”고 했다. 그러면서 “풍성한 숲을 이루려면 사슴과 꽃 등 다른 생태계 참여자도 중요하고 특히 토양인 데이터가 중요하다”며 “토양이 사실 모델의 지능에 좌우하는 결정적인 역할을 한다”고 강조했다. 공동연구소는 첫 단추로 내년까지 우리말에 최적화된 합성 데이터세트 100만 건을 구축해 공유한다. 김 소장은 “한국의 인구통계학적·지리적·문화적 특성을 반영해 만든 엔비디아 페르소나 데이터세트가 공개된 후 얼마나 인기를 끌었는지를 보면 한국 연구자가 얼마나 양질의 우리말 데이터를 기다려 왔는지 알 수 있다”고 했다. 연구소는 글 데이터를 시작으로 향후 피지컬AI용과 기업에 특화한 데이터로 영역을 확장할 방침이다. 공동연구소는 엔비디아의 글로벌 연구개발 조직인 엔비디아 리서치 소속이다. 현재 10명 규모의 인턴과 엔비디아 정규직이 될 연구원을 채용하고 있다. 글로벌 AI 빅테크 중 핵심 연구 조직에서 한국인 정규직 연구자를 채용하는 건 엔비디아가 처음이다. 허진 기자 hjin@hankyung.com

headlines.body: In June 2013, President Barack Obama welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Sunnylands, a secluded California estate, for an informal summit. Behind the diplomatic pleasantries, Obama confronted Xi over Chinese state-directed cyber-enabled espionage and theft of American intellectual property, warning that such activities threatened American companies and the broader bilateral relationship. Thirteen years after the Sunnylands Summit, the threat has evolved significantly as the race to dominate AI frames the U.S.-China relationship. The stakes are higher, the technology more consequential, and the vulnerabilities increasingly involve attempts to compromise or coopt the "key man" at the helm of the nation's top technology companies. With the unfolding scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the blame should start with the CEO himself, but it should not end there. The situation illustrates a failure of Silicon Valley, corporate and political leadership at a much wider level. Huang has acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman identified in reporting as Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. American intelligence officials reportedly believe she was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information and potentially influence Nvidia's efforts to loosen American semiconductor export restrictions. China denies the allegations. Nvidia's independent directors have launched an investigation, and so far, they say no compromise of company secrets or national security information has been established. But the problem extends well beyond Huang or Nvidia. Focusing exclusively on whether proprietary technology or trade secrets were transferred fundamentally misunderstands the potential intelligence value of such an operation. For Beijing, gaining insight into, influencing, or potentially compromising American technology policymaking could be equally valuable. Advance knowledge of export-control deliberations, regulatory intentions, negotiating positions, or divisions within the administration could provide strategic advantages without a single semiconductor design being stolen. The Trump administration reportedly received warnings about the relationship before the scandal became public. Nevertheless, Huang remained an influential participant in semiconductor policy discussions while advocating greater access to China's market. New reporting also raises questions about interactions between Nvidia and Commerce Department officials during an investigation into Megaspeed, subsequently transferred to the Justice Department. No improper influence has been established, but corporate access to government decision-making deserves scrutiny alongside proprietary technology. It is a new era of 'key man' risk with AI Whether appropriate protective measures were taken remains unclear. headlines.body: Nvidia's board of directors said on Tuesday that it hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang and whether company secrets or national security was compromised, after Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who has been connected to Chinese intelligence. "The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday," the board said in a statement. Kim joined the firm last month, and he was previously the chief U.S. prosecutor in Manhattan, according to Law360. Nvidia has been thrust into turmoil since Huang's acknowledgement of the affair over the weekend. The chipmaker's stock dropped 6% on Tuesday after falling more than 4% on Monday, as investors worry that the investigation and scandal could result in the co-founder and CEO being forced out. Nvidia and the board are facing pressure from critics and politicians over what the company knew about sales of its restricted AI chips to Chinese companies. Over the past few weeks, The New York Times and Financial Times have reported that U.S. intelligence agencies surveilled an Asian technology executive, Alice Huang, who has been affiliated with Nvidia customer Megaspeed. These agencies have concluded that she is passing information to Beijing and is involved with Chinese intelligence, according to the reports. Huang has become the face of the AI industry, going by his first name "Jensen" to customers and rivals as Nvidia's technology is used to train nearly all major AI models. The chipmaker has become an essential source of financing for AI startups and Huang has met with presidents and CEOs around the world as Nvidia's public face. But Huang's actions have thrown the chipmaker into instability as he admitted to an affair with Alice Huang in an email to staff on Sunday. "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message, while emphasizing that he is an American and supports U.S. national security. An Nvidia representative said at the time that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption. On Sunday, Nvidia's board said that it would investigate the allegations that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Nvidia's board also said on Sunday that it has no reason to believe either national security nor Nvidia secrets were compromised. This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.

headlines.body: TensorBay has launched a containerized AI offering. Dubbed AIPods, the 1MW containerized nodes can support up to 64 Nvidia HGX B300 systems and can be deployed in 12 weeks. The AIPods combine the hardware with a distributed private inference platform and include the Nvidia Dynamo-based inference optimization, including KV-aware routing and disaggregated serving. In a LinkedIn post announcing the launch, TensorBay said: “The real breakthrough isn’t simply putting GPUs inside a container. It’s making geographically distributed AI capacity operate as a coordinated inference platform. “Instead of concentrating everything in one massive facility, enterprises can deploy capacity closer to their users, expand region by region, retain control over their models and data, and reduce dependence on centralized third-party inference providers.” Headquartered in San Jose, California, TensorBay offers access to AI infrastructure from Tier III data centers in the US, Brazil, Europe, and Asia Pacific, with five locations operating. It claims to have more than 24,000 GPUs operating across its footprint. A number of companies offer containerized AI solutions. Last month, LG launched an AI Box offering, and ZTE also has a small AI container solution.

headlines.body: CoreWeave reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and lifted its 2026 guidance on Tuesday, showing that demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remains strong despite concerns of a market slowdown. The stock advanced in extended trading. The earnings announcement lands at a particularly volatile moment for CoreWeave and its neocloud peers, as the market sours on the AI trade and as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the central figure in the global buildout, faces a scandal tied to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: - Loss per share: 95 cents adjusted vs. $1.16 expected - Revenue: $3.66 billion vs. $3.55 billion expected CoreWeave's revenue soared 168% from about $1.36 billion a year earlier, according to a statement. The company recorded a net loss of $709 million, or $1.27 per share, compared to a net loss of $110 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings exclude stock-based compensation. Executives pushed up their forecast for 2026. They now see $1.275 billion to $1.375 billion in adjusted operating income on $13 billion to $13.3 billion in revenue. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha were looking for $1.07 billion in adjusted operating income, and analysts polled by LSEG had expected $12.86 billion in 2026 revenue. In August, CoreWeave's 2026 guidance included $960 million to $1.15 billion in adjusted operating income and $12.4 billion to $13.2 billion in revenue. CoreWeave has lost over 40% of its value in the past month, as investors rotate out of companies most closely tied to AI infrastructure. Rising interest rates have pushed lenders out of the market, raising concerns about ongoing access to capital. Some CoreWeave bond yields recently topped 16%. "The business can execute well and still face a tougher financing environment," Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, wrote in an email. "Strong demand is encouraging; the cost and availability of capital remain critical." CoreWeave will get most the capital it needs for 2027 through clients pre-payments and financing from hardware partners, and the company will raise "a limited amount" as well, CEO Mike Intrator told analysts on a conference call. The company plans to raise new debt tied to a set of contracts in the weeks to come, said Nitin Agrawal, its finance chief. "At current yields, we do not intend to issue additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027," he said. "By contrast, the asset-level secured debt market has remained stable, with our loans continuing to trade around par value." In all, he said he projects under $5 billion in parent-level debt financing through 2027. Fellow neocloud Nebius, whose stock is down by a similar amount, is scheduled to report earnings on Thursday. Nebius shares got a small boost from CoreWeave's results. README:  # Nemotron 3 Diarization ## Description **[Nemotron 3 Diarization](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/nemotron-diarization)** is an open-weight speaker diarization model designed to determine "who spoke when" in real-world audio. It supports both streaming and offline inference and handles up to eight speakers. Following Sortformer [\[1\]](#ref-1), the model resolves speaker permutation by ordering its output channels according to each speaker's first arrival in the input audio. For streaming inference, the model adopts the Arrival-Order Speaker Cache (AOSC) and FIFO queue introduced in **Streaming Sortformer** [\[2\]](#ref-2). The AOSC retains speaker information from earlier chunks to preserve speaker identities over time, while the FIFO queue provides recent frame context for each processing step. A single checkpoint supports input buffer latency as low as 80 ms for latency-critical applications, although the lowest recommended configuration is 0.32 s; the offline-style configuration uses a 30.4 s input buffer. The output frame resolution is configurable in multiples of 10 ms.
